title: Nayi Chetna 5.0 to be Launched on 25 November
subtitle: Joint Inter-Ministerial Advisory involving 15 Ministries/Departments and Signed Quadripartite MoU on Violence-Free Village Initiative to be Unveiled
body_text: The Ministry of Rural Development will launch the fifth edition of its national gender campaign, Nayi Chetna – Pahal Badlav Ki, on 25 November 2026, marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women . The month-long campaign will be implemented nationwide from 25 November to 23 December 2026 under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Hon’ble Union Minister of Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, will inaugurate the national launch in the presence of Smt. Annpurna Devi, Hon’ble Union Minister of Women and Child Development; Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Law and Justice; and Hon’ble Mr Justice Vikram Nath, Judge, Supreme Court of India and Executive Chairman, National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The event will also witness the presence of Shri Kamlesh Paswan, Hon’ble Minister of State, Rural Development, and Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Hon’ble Minister of State for Rural Development and Communications, along with senior officials of participating Ministries, representatives of State Governments, development partners and women leaders from community institutions across the country. The launch will take place at 4:00 PM at Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, NASC Complex, Dev Prakash Shastri Marg, Pusa, New Delhi – 110012 . The theme of Nayi Chetna 5.0, “ From Access to Agency: Empowering Women through Livelihoods and Equal Opportunities for a Viksit Bharat,” highlights the importance of women’s access and mobility as critical enablers of economic empowerment, livelihood participation and independent decision-making. Four interconnected areas of focus Nayi Chetna 5.0 will place women’s economic empowerment at the centre of its approach, with a focus on four interconnected areas: recognising women as economic contributors, strengthening women’s access to and control over assets, promoting safe mobility, and redistributing unpaid care work. Particular emphasis will be placed on addressing barriers that restrict women’s access to livelihood opportunities, markets, financial services, public spaces and essential services, and their ability to move freely, safely and independently. The campaign aims to move beyond awareness generation towards coordinated action and measurable improvements in women’s economic participation, agency and decision-making. The highlights of the event Joint Inter-Ministerial Advisory involving 15 Ministries/Departments A key highlight of the national launch will be the release of a Joint Inter-Ministerial Advisory involving 15 Ministries/Departments. The Advisory will reflect a shared commitment to advance the objectives of Nayi Chetna 5.0 through coordinated action and convergence. It will provide a framework for Ministries and Departments to align their schemes, programmes, institutional mechanisms and frontline networks with the campaign’s objectives. It will seek to strengthen coordinated interventions at the national, State, district and community levels, particularly to improve women’s access to livelihoods, assets, financial services, safe mobility, essential services and institutional support. Signed Quadripartite MoU on Violence-Free Village Initiative The event will also feature the release of the signed Quadripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the Violence-Free Village Initiative, among the Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Women and Child Development, Department of Justice and National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The MoU will provide a framework for coordinated institutional action to prevent and respond to gender-based violence at the community level. It is intended to strengthen convergence between community institutions, legal services authorities and relevant government mechanisms, including awareness of legal rights, access to justice, institutional support and collective action towards building violence-free villages. Strengthening community institutions and women’s leadership DAY-NRLM’s extensive network of Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Village Organisations (VOs), Cluster Level Federations (CLFs), Gender Resource Centres (GRCs) and other community institutions will play a central role in the implementation of Nayi Chetna 5.0. During the launch, new Gender Resource Centres will be inaugurated as community-level platforms to facilitate access to services, entitlements, support systems and grievance redressal mechanisms. SHG women leaders from different States will share their experiences, innovations and perspectives on strengthening women’s collective action and leadership. The programme will also feature two panel discussions during the day. The first panel, “Advancing Ministerial Convergence through Gender Resource Centres (GRCs), One Stop Centres (OSCs), Legal Services Authority (LSA), and Health System,” will bring together representatives from relevant Ministries and institutions to deliberate on strengthening convergence and coordinated responses to women’s concerns. The second panel, “Women Leaders from the Field: Experiences, Innovations and the Way Forward,” will provide a platform for grassroots women leaders to share their experiences and recommendations. Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report The Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report will be released during the national launch. The report will present the assessment of the previous edition and its key learnings to inform and strengthen future campaign interventions. The programme will also include the screening of State-level videos and presentations of good practices, highlighting community-led initiatives and approaches towards gender equality. Video resources developed for the campaign will also be launched. Spearheaded by DAY-NRLM, Ministry of Rural Development, Nayi Chetna has evolved since its inception in 2022 into a nationwide collective movement to address gender-based violence (GBV), challenge discriminatory social norms and advance gender equality. Through Nayi Chetna 5.0, the Ministry seeks to strengthen collective action among Ministries, State Governments, community institutions and other stakeholders to create an enabling environment for women’s economic participation, safety and agency. The campaign will also encourage the active engagement of men, boys and youth in challenging discriminatory social norms and promoting equality and shared responsibility. ******* PU
